extracted.intended_audience: project owners, Public Housing Agencies (PHAs), and tenants of HUD-assisted projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities (and HUD staff administering those programs)
extracted.subtask_short: HUD pet rules for elderly/disabled housing
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory requirements (24 CFR part 5, subpart C–E excerpts) governing development, content, notice, enforcement, and tenant/owner procedures for pet rules in HUD-assisted projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities, and related definitions and applicability provisions. Covers mandatory and discretionary rule elements, notice and consultation procedures, deposits/charges, violation/removal processes, and protections for pets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to tenants: required content
rubrics_metrics.description: During development of pet rules the project owner or PHA shall serve written notice on all tenants stating that: (1) tenants are permitted to own and keep common household pets in accordance with the pet rules; (2) assistance animals are excluded from these requirements; (3) tenants may request a copy of any current or proposed pet rule or amendment; and (4) tenants may request lease amendment to permit common household pets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must be served to tenants in occupancy at time of service; applicants offered a unit must be given the notice containing items (1),(2),(3). If a PHA chooses not to promulgate rules, notice served within 60 days of the effective date of this part and in accordance with normal notice procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of pet rules: inclusion of mandatory rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owners must prescribe reasonable rules to govern the keeping of common household pets; pet rules must include the mandatory rules described in §5.350 and may include other discretionary provisions as provided in §5.318.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs may choose not to promulgate rules; if they do, they may base rules on §5.350 and may modify those provisions consistent with subpart C and applicable law. PHAs that do not promulgate rules shall not impose lease terms inconsistent with subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of discretion: reasonable relationship and narrow tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a project owner or PHA has discretion to prescribe pet rules, the pet rules should be reasonably related to furthering a legitimate interest of the owner or PHA and drawn narrowly to achieve those interests without imposing unnecessary burdens on pet owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate interests include providing a decent, safe, sanitary living environment, protecting project condition, and protecting the owner's financial interest. Owners/PHAs may vary rules by project or unit based on size, type, location, occupancy, provided rules are reasonable and do not conflict with state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict with State or local law
rubrics_metrics.description: The pet rules adopted shall not conflict with applicable State or local law or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict may exist, State and local law or regulations shall apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary rule factor: definition of 'common household pet'
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs may define 'common household pet' reasonably for Public Housing programs; project owners for Housing programs must use the Housing programs definition in §5.306.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of different definitions is allowed only as provided in the regulation (PHAs discretionary; project owners bound to §5.306 for Housing programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary rule factor: density of tenants and pets (unit limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may take into account tenant and pet density and place reasonable limitations on the number of common household pets allowed in each dwelling unit or group home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Housing programs project owners may limit four‑legged, warm‑blooded pets to one per dwelling unit or group home. Other than unit/group‑level limits described, pet rules may not limit the total number of pets allowed in the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary rule factor: group home definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Group home means, for Housing programs, a small communal living arrangement for persons who are chronically mentally ill, developmentally disabled, or physically disabled requiring continual supportive services (other than continual nursing, medical or psychiatric care); for Public Housing programs it means dwelling(s) for elderly persons or persons with disabilities who require planned continual supportive services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions inform application of density/limitation rules in paragraphs concerning group homes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary rule factor: pet size and type limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may place reasonable limitations on the size, weight, and type of common household pets allowed in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits must be reasonable and consistent with the discretion permitted in subpart C and not conflict with state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential financial obligations: refundable pet deposits (Housing programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may require tenants who own or keep pets to pay a refundable pet deposit; for project owners this deposit shall be limited to tenants who own or keep cats or dogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit is additional to other tenant financial obligations; may be used only to pay reasonable expenses directly attributable to presence of the pet (repairs, replacements, fumigation, animal care facilities). Unused portion must be refunded within a reasonable time after tenant moves or no longer owns/keeps the pet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum pet deposit: HUD-established limits for certain tenants
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet deposits for tenants whose rents are subsidized or who live in assisted projects shall not exceed amounts periodically fixed by HUD through notice; for all other tenants of projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities, deposit shall not exceed one month's rent at time the pet is brought onto premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In establishing maximums HUD will consider projected expenses, owners' ability to offset expenses, and low income status of tenants. For certain deposits HUD requires gradual accumulation with initial payment not to exceed $50 and monthly payments not to exceed $10 until reached; rules may allow gradual accumulation for other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Housing programs: maximum pet deposit rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum pet deposit a PHA may charge per dwelling unit shall not exceed the higher of the Total Tenant Payment or a reasonable fixed amount as the PHA may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pet rules may permit gradual accumulation of the pet deposit by the pet owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waste removal charge (Housing programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may permit a separate waste removal charge of up to five dollars ($5) per occurrence on pet owners that fail to remove pet waste in accordance with prescribed pet rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any waste removal charge within the $5 limitation is deemed reasonable for purposes of subpart C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited financial obligations (insurance, strict liability, indemnity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owners or PHAs may not prescribe pet rules that impose additional financial obligations designed to compensate for costs associated with pets, including requiring liability insurance, strict liability where not imposed by state/local law, or indemnification for pet-related litigation and attorneys' fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions are only as provided in paragraph (d) for Housing programs and applicable references for Public Housing programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of pet care: limited to necessary protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may prescribe standards of pet care and handling limited to those necessary to protect the tenant's unit and project premises or to protect health/safety of tenants, employees, and the public; rules may not require removal of a pet's vocal cords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted rules include barring pets from specified common areas unless exclusion denies reasonable ingress/egress; requiring control of noise and odor; for Housing programs, may require spay/neuter and limit time pet may be left unattended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pet licensing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may require pet owners to license pets in accordance with applicable State and local laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of pet rules to include licensing requirement does not relieve pet owners of responsibility to comply with state/local licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated pet/no-pet areas (Public Housing)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs may designate buildings, floors, or sections as no-pet areas or designate sections for pet‑owning tenants; PHAs may direct initial tenant moves to establish these areas and may adjust areas or direct additional moves to accommodate applicants or changing needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs may not refuse or delay admission because an applicant's admission would violate a pet/no‑pet area. Project owners may not designate pet areas in their pet rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary visiting pets exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules may exclude from the project pets not owned by a tenant that are to be kept temporarily (less than 14 consecutive days and nights) on the premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD encourages project owners and PHAs to permit visiting pet programs sponsored by humane societies or nonprofits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease provisions: required statements (§5.321)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases for tenants of projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities must: (i) state tenants are permitted to keep common household pets (subject to subpart and pet rules); (ii) incorporate by reference the pet rules; (iii) state the tenant agrees to comply; and (iv) state violation of the rules may be grounds for removal of the pet or termination of tenancy (or both) in accordance with subpart and applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a PHA has not established pet rules, leases shall not contain provisions prohibiting owning/keeping common household pets and must state that such owning/keeping is subject to general lease obligations and applicable state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of lease provisions (timing of inclusion/amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases for tenants admitted on or after implementation must contain §5.321 provisions; leases for existing tenants must be amended to include §5.321 provisions upon renewal (Housing) or annual reexamination/when tenant wishes to own a pet (Public Housing) or when tenant registers a pet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific triggers differ by Housing vs Public Housing programs as described in §5.324.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuisance or threat to health or safety removal authority (§5.327)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owner, PHA, or appropriate community authority may require removal of any pet if the pet's conduct or condition is duly determined under state/local law to constitute a nuisance or threat to health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in subpart C limits state/local authorities or owners/PHAs from requiring removal under applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pet rules: inoculations (§5.350(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules shall require pet owners to have their pets inoculated in accordance with State and local laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification of inoculations is required in pet registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pet rules: sanitary standards (§5.350(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules shall prescribe sanitary standards governing disposal of pet waste, which may include designating exercise/waste deposit areas, forbidding exercise or waste outside designated areas, requiring owners to remove and properly dispose of removable pet waste, and requiring owners to remove pets to exercise or deposit waste if no area designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For cats and pets using litter boxes, rules may require changing litter (but not more than twice each week), separating pet waste from litter (but not more than once each day), and prescribe disposal methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pet rules: pet restraint (§5.350(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules shall require that all cats and dogs be appropriately and effectively restrained and under the control of a responsible individual while on the common areas of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraint requirements apply to common areas of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory pet rules: registration (§5.350(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pet rules shall require pet owners to register their pets before bringing them onto project premises and to update registration at least annually; registration must include veterinarian certificate of required inoculations, information sufficient to identify the pet and show it is a common household pet, and names/contacts of responsible parties to care for the pet if owner dies or is incapacitated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project owner may require additional info to ensure compliance with discretionary rules and require pet owner to sign statement indicating they have read and agree to comply. Owner may refuse registration for enumerated reasons but may not refuse based on owner's financial inability or therapeutic value considerations. Refusal must be accompanied by written notice stating basis and served per §5.353(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for development: notice of proposed pet rules (§5.353(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owners shall develop proposed pet rules and serve notice on each tenant including the text of proposed rules, a statement that tenants or representatives may submit written comments, and that comments must be submitted no later than 30 days from the notice effective date; notice may announce meeting date/time/place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow service procedures in paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenant consultation procedures (§5.353(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Tenants or tenant representatives may submit written comments and may attend owner‑scheduled meetings to make oral comments; owner must consider only comments made at meetings if they are summarized, reduced to writing, and submitted prior to end of comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may schedule one or more meetings during the comment period to discuss proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development and notice of final pet rules (§5.353(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing tenants' written comments and meeting summaries, project owner shall develop final rules; content of final rules is within sole discretion of owner (subject to subpart C). The owner must serve notice of final rules to each tenant including the text and effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may meet with tenants to attempt to resolve issues; final content remains within owner's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of pet rules (§5.353(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Project owner may amend pet rules at any time by following the development procedures for proposed and final rules specified in paragraphs (b) through (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments require same notice, comment period, and final notice procedures as initial rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of notice methods and effectiveness (§5.353(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The project owner must serve notices by: (i) first class mail to tenant's dwelling unit; (ii) serving a copy on any adult answering the door or placing the notice under/through the door if no adult responds; or (iii) for high‑rise buildings, posting the notice in at least three conspicuous places and maintaining posted notices for 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For computing time periods, service is effective on the day all notices are delivered or mailed, or posted (for posting the effective day is the initial posting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pet rule violation notice requirements (§5.356(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner determines, on basis of objective facts supported by written statements, that a pet owner has violated a rule, owner may serve a written notice of pet rule violation that must: (1) contain brief factual basis and rule alleged violated; (2) state pet owner has 10 days from effective service date to correct violation or request meeting; (3) state pet owner can be accompanied by another person at meeting; and (4) state failure to correct/request/appear may result in initiation of procedures to terminate tenancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations must be based on objective facts supported by written statements; service per §5.353(f)(1)(i) or (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pet rule violation meeting procedures (§5.356(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If pet owner timely requests a meeting, project owner shall set mutually agreeable time/place no later than 15 days from effective date of notice to discuss alleged violation and attempt to correct it; owner may grant additional time to correct as result of meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meetings allow discussion and may lead to additional corrective time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice for pet removal (§5.356(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner and pet owner cannot resolve violation or owner determines pet owner failed to correct within additional time, owner may serve written notice requiring removal of the pet that must: (i) contain brief factual basis and rule violated; (ii) state owner must remove pet within 10 days of effective date of notice (or meeting if notice served there); and (iii) state failure to remove may result in initiation of tenancy termination procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service methods as per §5.353(f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on initiating tenancy termination for pet violations (§5.356(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may not initiate procedures to terminate tenancy based on a pet rule violation unless: (i) pet owner has failed to remove or correct violation within applicable time (including additional time if provided); and (ii) the pet rule violation is sufficient to begin termination procedures under the lease and applicable regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may initiate pet removal under §5.327 at any time, consistent with state/local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rejection of units near pets (§5.359)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may reject a unit offered if it is in close proximity to a unit where an existing tenant owns or keeps a common household pet; such rejection shall not adversely affect the applicant's application status, waiting list position, or tenant selection preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners are not required to provide alternate units because of proximity of pets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional lease provisions: inspections (§5.360(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Leases may state that project owner may, after reasonable notice and during reasonable hours, enter and inspect premises if owner has received a signed written complaint alleging or has reasonable grounds to believe that a pet's conduct or condition constitutes a nuisance or threat to health or safety under state/local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections in addition to other permitted inspections must be tied to complaints or reasonable grounds related to pet conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional lease provisions: emergencies and removal (§5.360(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If no state/local authority is authorized to remove a vicious or severely ill pet, the project owner may include lease language permitting entry and removal of the pet and taking permissible actions (including placing it in a care facility up to 30 days); owner may act only after requesting owner to remove pet and refusal or inability to contact owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease may not relieve owner from liability for wrongful removal. Costs of animal care facility borne as provided in §5.363.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of the pet when owner incapacitated (§5.363)
rubrics_metrics.description: If pet's health or safety is threatened by death/incapacity of owner, project owner may contact responsible parties listed in registration; if they cannot care for pet, owner may contact state/local authority for removal; if no authority exists and lease permits, owner may enter unit, remove pet, and place it in facility for up to 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost of animal care facility is borne by pet owner and if unable/unwilling to pay may be paid from pet deposit if imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Housing programs: PHA tenant consultation and HUD reporting (§5.380)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs that promulgate pet rules shall consult with tenants of projects for the elderly or persons with disabilities and develop procedures giving tenants adequate opportunity to review/comment before issuance; PHAs are solely responsible for final content but must give consideration to tenant comments and send copies of final/amended rules and summaries/copies of tenant comments to responsible HUD field office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PHAs must develop specific tenant consultation procedures designed to give adequate opportunity to review and comment; PHAs remain responsible for content but must consider comments and report to HUD field office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to pet rule application (Subpart D excerpts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms used in HUD programs (e.g., Annual Contributions Contract (ACC), Applicant, Disabled family, Displaced family, Elderly family, Family, Live-in aide, Near-elderly family, Person with disabilities) that determine program applicability, tenant categories, and procedural rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory/regulatory definitions affect who is covered by the pet rules and the application of subparts C–E to various households and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart E applicability: covered programs and individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart E implements Section 214 (prohibiting HUD financial assistance to persons not in eligible status) and applies to listed programs including Section 235, Section 236 (certain tenants), Rent Supplement Program, HUD's Public Housing Programs, Section 8 Programs, and Housing Development Grant Programs (with respect to low-income units).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions apply to both applicants and persons already receiving assistance, and to covered entities (PHAs, project owners, mortgagees under Section 235).
